title: Prefill-Decode Orchestrator with Kernel-aware Admission for Tail Latency
creator: Anjali Mehta
description: Background: Continuous batching has reduced average cost but p99 tail latency remains elevated for mixed prefill+decode workloads. Root causes identified in recent traces: long prefill requests blocking decode admission, suboptimal kernel choices for heterogeneous batch shapes, and KV cache thrashing on long sequence prefixes. Goal: implement a coordinator that (1) separates admission budgeting for prefill vs decode, (2) selects kernels not just by throughput but by tail-latency sensitivity, and (3) schedules prefill/decodes to minimize long-tail outliers while preserving overall throughput.
proposed_solution: 1) Admission budget: implement a headroom token budget per worker that reserves N% capacity for short-latency decodes. 2) Kernel-aware admission: annotate model variants/kernels with latency-profile tags (low-latency, high-throughput) and prefer low-latency kernels when serving tail-sensitive decodes. 3) Prefill shaping: group prefill requests by prefix-length bucket and do 'prefix-merge' to avoid duplicate KV work; evict/compact KV entries using time-aware LRU to reduce thrash. 4) Decode preemption: allow small decodes to preempt a prefill microbatch if headroom is exhausted, by splitting prefill into finer microbatches. 5) Fallback policy: when a low-latency kernel is unavailable, route to a compatible smaller-variant model or apply quantization-mode fallback only for short decodes. 6) Observability: add per-route headroom metrics and a canary dashboard tracking p50/p95/p99 for prefill vs decode separately.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for decode-only requests reduced by >=40% on mixed workload (measured on benchmark rig)
overall throughput regression <=2% for typical RLHF-like mixes
canary rollout with 5% traffic for 72h with no increase in error rate or SLO violations
automated unit and integration tests for admission bookkeeping and kernel-selection fallback
deployment toggles to tune headroom fraction and kernel preference per tenant
updates: 2025-11-04: Ticket opened after incident review of 2025-11-02 where p99 spiked to 1.2s for mixed workloads.
2025-11-10: Prototype admission headroom implemented in dev branch; initial microbench shows p99 decode improvement on single-worker tests.
2025-11-18: Kernel tagging added to model manifest. Bench harness extended to record kernel latency distributions by sequence length.
2025-11-24: Prefill prefix-merge algorithm implemented; observed 12% reduction in redundant KV prefill ops in local simulation.
2025-11-29: Integration test flake fixed by Alejandro; preparing RFC for runtime config knobs and rollout plan.
2025-12-02: Canary PR submitted (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4213); seeking review from @mira and @sachin before staging deploy.
benchmarks: Baseline mixed workload (seq=1024, mix=60% prefill+40% decode): p99 decode=420ms, p95=160ms
After prefix-merge+headroom (single-worker g4dn-12xlarge): p99 decode=240ms (-43%), p95=120ms (-25%), throughput -1.7%
blockers: Need kernel-latency annotations on model manifest (owner: model-onboarding team)
RBAC change for tenant-level headroom override requires security signoff
acceptance_tests: Canary at 5% traffic for 72h with p99 decode improvement and no error-rate increase
Synthetic mix replay in benchmark rig reproduces >=40% p99 improvement
notes_on_tradeoffs: Reserving headroom reduces available throughput for large prefill bursts; we mitigate with finer-grained microbatching and temporary throughput drop allowance
Preferring low-latency kernels may increase cost; expose knob per tenant to balance cost vs latency
Kernel fallback to smaller model variant risks output quality divergence — restrict to short decodes and add eval gating
